title: Pinned posts with a per-profile limit
name: Profile pinned posts

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code enforces the limit of three pinned posts under concurrent requests? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: There is none. The count-then-update in pin() is a classic write-skew pattern, but it runs under SERIALIZABLE. If two pin() calls for the same author both read a count of 2 and each updates a different post, PostgreSQL's serializable snapshot isolation detects the read/write dependency cycle and aborts one with 40001. withTransaction rolls back, waits, and retries; on retry the count is 3 and PinLimitError is thrown. Each attempt uses a fresh connection and the error is rethrown once attempts are exhausted.

choiceQuestions.prompt: An author has 2 pinned posts. Two pin() calls for two different posts run at the same time. What is the outcome?
choices: Both succeed and the author ends up with 4 pinned posts
Exactly one succeeds; the other is retried and then fails with PinLimitError
Both fail with a serialization error returned to the caller
One succeeds and the other blocks until the first commits, then succeeds too
choiceQuestions.explanation: Under SERIALIZABLE, the two transactions read overlapping rows (the count) and each writes a row the other read, so one is aborted with 40001. withTransaction retries it; the fresh attempt sees 3 pinned and throws PinLimitError, which is not retryable. Four pins would need a weaker isolation level, the error is not surfaced because it is retried, and serializable checks do not simply block-and-proceed.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Inside the work callback, PinLimitError is thrown. What does withTransaction do?
choices: Retries up to maxAttempts because any error inside the callback is retried
Commits the transaction and then rethrows
Rolls back, releases the client, and rethrows immediately
Leaves the transaction open on the client so the caller can inspect it
choiceQuestions.explanation: The catch block always runs ROLLBACK, and since PinLimitError has no 40001/40P01 code, retryable is false and it is rethrown; finally releases the client. Only serialization and deadlock errors are retried, COMMIT is skipped because the throw happens before it, and the client is never handed back mid-transaction.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why does listPinned() use pool.query directly instead of withTransaction?
choices: It is a single read statement, which already sees one consistent snapshot, so an explicit transaction adds nothing
Because SERIALIZABLE transactions cannot run SELECT with ORDER BY
Because pool.query reads uncommitted pins from in-flight transactions
To bypass the row locks held by pin()
choiceQuestions.explanation: A single statement gets its own snapshot in PostgreSQL, so wrapping it in a transaction provides no extra consistency. SERIALIZABLE supports any SELECT, PostgreSQL never exposes uncommitted data, and plain reads are not blocked by row locks anyway.
